one_line: A fifth‑century Kannada court scribe overseeing the landmark Halmidi land‑grant inscription in the Kadamba–Ganga world.

appearance.age_look: Mid-20s to early 30s, slim but sturdy build, average height with a slightly scholarly posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp black eyes under slightly arched brows, a small tilaka of pale sandal paste on the forehead, and a calm, focused default expression that softens into a hint of pride.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled tightly back into a short, neat topknot at the back of the crown, sides and back trimmed close but not shaved, with a simple narrow white cotton headband tied around the head just above the knot.
appearance.costume: Era-appropriate early historic Deccan attire: a long-sleeved, thigh-length off-white cotton tunic (angarakha-style overlap to the right, tied inside and outside with thin cords) worn over a ankle-length dull-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated in front, edge bordered with a narrow dark-green stripe; a soft, medium-length pale-cream uttariya scarf with a faint reddish-brown woven border draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back; simple brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery consisting of a single thin copper bangle on the right wrist and small round copper ear-studs, plus a modest palm-leaf manuscript roll tied at the waist with a plain brown cord.
appearance.signature: A rectangular, grey stone inscription-slab held upright at his side with faintly carved early Kannada lines, accompanied by a slender stylus-like iron chisel in his right hand used to guide stone-cutters.

ref_desc: A lean, medium-brown young male scribe with sharp black eyes, black hair in a short topknot and white headband, wearing an off-white long-sleeved tunic, dull-ochre dhoti with dark-green border, pale-cream uttariya, simple copper jewellery, and holding a grey stone inscription-slab and slim iron chisel.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a fifth-century South Indian Kannada court scribe: a lean, medium-brown young man with an oval face, sharp black eyes, straight nose, and a small sandalwood tilaka, his default expression calm and focused with a hint of pride. His thick black hair is pulled into a short, neat topknot at the back of the crown, with the sides and back trimmed close, and a narrow white cotton headband wraps around his head just above the knot. Dress him in an early Deccan outfit: a long-sleeved, thigh-length off-white cotton tunic overlapping and tied to the right, over an ankle-length dull-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped and tightly pleated in front, its edge marked with a narrow dark-green stripe. Drape a soft pale-cream uttariya scarf with a faint reddish-brown border from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, and put simple brown leather sandals on his feet. Add minimal accessories: a thin copper bangle on his right wrist, small round copper ear-studs, and a modest palm-leaf manuscript roll tied at his waist with a plain brown cord. In his right hand he holds a slender stylus-like iron chisel used to guide stone-cutters, and at his side he steadies a rectangular grey stone inscription-slab carved with faint early Kannada lines. Use a palette of off-white, dull ochre, dark green, pale cream, and stone grey, and show front, three-quarter, and back views to clearly display his consistent face, hair, clothing, and signature stone slab with chisel.
